title: Functor
description: JSON Schema for a functor — a structure-preserving map F: C -> D between two categories (Mac Lane 1971 Ch. I §3; Awodey 2010 §1.3). A functor sends objects of C to objects of D and morphisms of C to morphisms of D, preserving composition (F(g compose f) = F(g) compose F(f)) and identities (F(id_A) = id_{F(A)}). The schema captures the data: the source-category name, target-category name, object-map (a map from source-object names to target-object names), and morphism-map (a map from source-morphism names to target-morphism names). The preservation laws are universally-quantified equations checked by functoriality transformers, not by JSON Schema.

source-category.description: The name of the source category C.

target-category.description: The name of the target category D.

object-map.description: F_obj: Ob(C) -> Ob(D). Map from a source-category object's name to its image — a target-category object's name. Every key and value satisfies name-shape; both are referenced via $dynamicRef.

morphism-map.description: F_mor: Hom_C -> Hom_D. Map from a source-category morphism's name to its image — a target-category morphism's name. Every key and value satisfies name-shape; both are referenced via $dynamicRef.
